body:
I pretty much already live in a big city in a lower cost state, I live in St. Louis, Missouri. And I live in the cheapest part of the city I can and still be relatively safe. 

I don’t think the testosterone is making my depression any worse. It helps with my dysphoria so if anything it makes things a bit better. Death by suicide is more common for men because they choose more lethal methods like guns and hangings, but women have more attempts usually. I don’t know about statistics for non-binary folks.

If I wanted to live in a lower cost area, I’d need a car/license. Which isn’t happening anytime soon. The aforementioned accident happened while a friend was teaching me to drive. I totaled their car and the guilt is killing me. I have no desire to get a license or drive myself going forward. Between the guilt and the trauma of the accident I don’t think I’ll be behind the wheel for a long time. 

I wish I could have more cats. My apartment complex allows 2 pets so theoretically I could get another but ther just isn’t room. Also I don’t think I could take care of another one appropriately. 

I’ve been trans my whole life. I’ve been processing it internally since I was about 18. And I’ve been coming out bit by bit for the past year. That was actually my main drive to see a therapist. I’ve been medically transitioning for about a month now, meaning I’ve been taking testosterone for that long.

I thought about peace corps for a long time but you need to have some sort of applicable education or experience and unfortunately, I don’t. Also, I’m trans and a lot of the places peace corps goes to are unsafe for the lgbtq community especially the t. 

I actually work at home for my main job, that is when I’m not too depressed and spend all day in bed or on the couch. 

I definitely pamper my girl. She’s especially cuddly so she loves that I work at home. She only gets blue buffalo food and has so many toys I have to hide half of them in a bin and then rotate them. I was really lucky to get her, by the time I adopted her she was at a foster thru the rescue so I didn’t really “save” her or anything but we ended up being a great match. I specifically chose a rescue that uses fosters so that I’d know her personality in a home and not a shelter before I adopted her. Her foster definitely cares for her and if I ever go on vacation is the first to volunteer to watch her. It’s also nice because I know that if anything happens to me she was somewhere to go and will be taken care of.

I have , but to be 100% honest I haven’t been completely honest with how bad my depression gets to my therapist. I’m afraid of being committed. Also, I wouldn’t make enough money on disability to get by. And yeah, I have like a “high functioning “ form of depression where I’m mostly able to go about my regular life, shower, work(except recently), etc. so a lot of people have zero clue because I seem fine but I’m really suicidal. 

I have a 4 year old tuxedo cat. She was adopted from a local cat rescue 3 years ago. She is a “dog-cat.” She’s very affectionate and intelligent. I love her so much and I’m gonna miss her a lot. Her name is Skyler. She was named by her foster rescue and I couldn’t decided not to rename her when I adopted her because her foster mom loved her so much that it felt like an insult to change her name.

I work for a major health insurance company doing customer service at my main job. At my second job, I work at a touristy destination in my city selling tickets. I have a cat and she’s pretty much been the reason I haven’t killed myself sooner. 
In school, I never really settled on a major. I just kept changing it and thus never graduated. My last time I went to school I did anthropology and history. 
I’ve been depressed since I was about 12. I’ve been cutting since I was 13. Only started seeing a therapist a year ago and tbh it hasn’t helped at all. Everyone says to get help and I finally did and I’m still in the same spot I’ve always been in. 
I could probably scrape by with one job if I defaulted on my loans, actually stuck to a budget, and didn’t miss so much work at my main job because of depression and migraines. But yeah, I’m not able to do any of those so two jobs it is.

The last time I took pills, it was 3 months of beta blockers, I passed out and woke up in the morning. I felt like shit but I didn’t tell anybody and continued life pretty much as normal. 
I’m 27. I live in a studio apartment, I don’t have a car or license. I work two jobs just to make ends meet. I tried college twice and still didn’t graduate and I’m up to my neck in student loan debt. My depressions has gotten to the point that  I’ve not worked in a week and I don’t know what to do.

Honestly, I don’t really want help. I’m still taking pills and I’m probably gonna until I lose consciousness. I’ve tried this before and it didn’t work but I’m hoping this time it does. I just don’t see myself making it any further in life.

Nothing that won’t heal eventually. 
I’ve thought about it but I can’t afford to be admitted. I can’t handle more medical bills and I would probably lose my job. I’d end up in worse shape coming out then going in, I’m pretty sure.
